title: MACP Agent Bootstrap Payload
description: Canonical schema for the bootstrap payload written to MACP_BOOTSTRAP_FILE before an agent process is spawned. Consumed by the agent at startup to learn its session_id, participant_id, mode, runtime address + Bearer token, and — for the initiator agent only — the SessionStart payload and the first kickoff envelope template. Flat, snake_case top level: this is the shape every real producer emits and both SDK readers (macp-sdk-python's from_bootstrap(), macp-sdk-typescript's fromBootstrap()) accept. See direct-agent-auth architecture (§Invariants).

session_id.description: Pre-allocated session identifier the initiator will bind at SessionStart. Satisfies runtime validation: UUID v4/v7 or base64url 22+ chars.

participant_id.description: The agent's sender id. Must match the authenticated identity on the runtime (RFC-MACP-0004 §4).

mode.description: Canonical mode identifier for the session this agent participates in (e.g. 'macp.mode.decision.v1').

runtime_url.description: gRPC endpoint of the MACP runtime, e.g. '127.0.0.1:50051' or 'runtime.internal:50051'. Alias of runtime_address; a caller sends one or the other (an empty string on the one present is treated as absent by both SDK readers, same as omitting it — hence the anyOf below is paired with minLength on both).

runtime_address.description: Alias of runtime_url, accepted by both SDK readers. Only runtime_url is emitted by the reference producer; runtime_address exists for callers that prefer that name.

auth_token.description: This agent's own Bearer token. Must match an identity in the runtime's MACP_AUTH_TOKENS_JSON whose 'sender' equals participant_id. When absent, the two SDK readers diverge, not fall back the same way: macp-sdk-typescript's runner always builds a dev-agent identity via Auth.devAgent(agent_id ?? participant_id) — see agent_id below; macp-sdk-python's runner only builds a dev-agent identity when agent_id (or the legacy auth alias's agent_id) is present, and otherwise leaves auth unset entirely.

agent_id.description: Agent catalog reference (e.g. 'fraud-agent'). Used only as an auth_token-absent dev-agent identity fallback, per both SDK readers. May equal participant_id.

secure.description: If true, use a secure (TLS) transport for the gRPC channel. Default true in production: RFC-MACP-0004 Section 2 (Transport Security) requires encrypted transport, and for gRPC over HTTP/2 requires TLS 1.2 or higher.

allow_insecure.description: Dev-only escape hatch permitting a plaintext channel. Must be false in production. NON-NORMATIVE note: within this bootstrap document the two fields are separate inputs -- secure states whether a secure transport is wanted, allow_insecure whether plaintext is tolerated -- but how an SDK combines them (whether allow_insecure alone may select plaintext, or only permit it) is NOT settled here. The two SDKs currently differ, and that default is each SDK's connection-security behavior, so it is theirs to reconcile; see the cross-SDK transport issue.

participants.description: Non-authoritative session-participant hint at the top level, distinct from initiator.session_start.participants (the authoritative list the initiator sends). Used by agent frameworks for display/setup only.

mode_version.description: Non-authoritative mode-version hint at the top level, distinct from initiator.session_start.mode_version.

configuration_version.description: Non-authoritative configuration-version hint at the top level, distinct from initiator.session_start.configuration_version.

policy_version.description: Non-authoritative policy-version hint at the top level, distinct from initiator.session_start.policy_version.

auth.description: Legacy alias accepted by macp-sdk-python's runner only, for backwards compatibility. The primary path — and what the reference producer emits — is the top-level auth_token field above.

initiator.description: Populated ONLY on the initiator agent's bootstrap. The initiator sends SessionStart using session_start, awaits ack, then emits kickoff (when present) as its first mode-scoped envelope.

ttl_ms.description: Session TTL in milliseconds. Mirrors macp-envelope.schema.json's SessionStartPayload.ttl_ms.

max_suspend_ms.description: Embedded as SessionStartPayload.max_suspend_ms when the initiator sends SessionStart. Upper bound on cumulative time the session may spend SUSPENDED (RFC-MACP-0001 §7.5). 0 or absent means the runtime's configured default.

context_id.description: Globally-unique context reference (e.g. ctx:sha256:<hex>, a URI, or any opaque string). The runtime preserves it but MUST NOT interpret it. Embedded as SessionStartPayload.context_id, a proto string, so this is a plain JSON string and is NOT base64-encoded.

extensions.description: Generic extension blocks keyed by protocol identifier. Embedded as SessionStartPayload.extensions, a map<string, bytes>; per RFC-MACP-0001 Section 10.3 protobuf bytes fields MUST be represented as base64-encoded strings in JSON. NON-NORMATIVE note on a cross-SDK divergence: macp-sdk-python's reader requires each value to be a string (tried as base64, falling back to raw UTF-8 bytes) and raises on any other JSON type; macp-sdk-typescript's reader accepts arbitrary JSON-serializable values and encodes them itself. This schema describes the narrower, Python-compatible shape — string-typed values — so a document validating here is guaranteed Python-safe but is not proof against a TypeScript-only value type (e.g. a JSON object or number) slipping through; see the cross-SDK extensions-typing issue.

additionalProperties.description: Protobuf bytes mapped to a base64 string in JSON (contentEncoding is an annotation in JSON Schema 2020-12, not an assertion: this schema declares the encoding, it does not validate it).

kickoff.description: Optional first mode-scoped envelope the initiator emits immediately after SessionStart is accepted (e.g., a Proposal for decision mode, a TaskRequest for task mode). May be absent for modes where the initiator opens the session but any participant may speak first.

payload_type.description: Emitted by the reference producer, but not read by either current SDK reader (declared-but-unmapped in macp-sdk-typescript, wholly unread in macp-sdk-python). Described here because the producer sends it; not to be relied on as consumed.

payload.description: The kickoff message's payload as a plain JSON object — every real producer and both SDKs' own documented examples send an object here, to be encoded onto Envelope.payload by the reader.

cancel_callback.description: Local HTTP endpoint the agent exposes so the control-plane's UI-cancel path (direct-agent-auth Option A) can ask the initiator to call CancelSession on the runtime with its own identity (RFC-MACP-0001 §7.2).

metadata.description: Free-form scenario metadata surfaced to the agent for framework setup (e.g. run_id, trace_id, scenario_ref, role, framework, agent_ref, policy_hints, session_context). Opaque to the runtime; not validated further here.
